title: Cross-country flight
topic: A friend subtracts local takeoff and landing times on a coast-to-coast flight
blurb: Takes off at 8:30 AM, lands at 5:00 PM — downloading four movies for an 8.5-hour flight.
prompt: A friend texted this while packing for a trip east. Tap a line if something doesn't add up, or call it clean.

segments.label: The ticket
segments.text: Booked a nonstop from San Francisco to Boston — takes off at 8:30 AM local and lands at 5:00 PM local.

segments.label: The clock
segments.text: Boston is three hours ahead of San Francisco, so I'm losing most of the afternoon once I land.

segments.label: The prep
segments.text: 8:30 to 5:00 is eight and a half hours in the air, so I'm downloading four movies for the flight.

segments.label: The seat
segments.text: At least I grabbed a window seat.

conclusion: 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM means 8.5 hours in the air, enough for four movies.

flaws.original: 8:30 AM in San Francisco is already 11:30 AM in Boston, so landing at 5:00 PM local is only 5.5 hours in the air, not 8.5.
flaws.corrupted: 8:30 to 5:00 is eight and a half hours in the air, so I'm downloading four movies for the flight.

diagnosis_choices.label: 8:30 AM in San Francisco is already 11:30 AM in Boston — you're only in the air for 5.5 hours, not 8.5.
Since Boston is 3 hours ahead, you have to add 3 hours to 8.5 — the flight is actually 11.5 hours.
8:30 AM to 5:00 PM is 9.5 hours, not 8.5, so four movies won't even cover it.
Boarding and taxiing eat an hour of the 8.5 hours, so you only get 7.5 hours of movie time.

fix_choices.label: Convert both clocks to Boston time (11:30 AM to 5:00 PM): it's a 5.5-hour flight, two movies tops.
Add the 3-hour jump for an 11.5-hour flight and download six movies.
Subtract an hour for boarding and taxiing to get 7.5 hours in the air.
Recount 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM as 9.5 hours and download a fifth movie.

flaws.explanation: 8:30 AM in San Francisco is already 11:30 AM in Boston. Those three missing hours are the time-zone jump, not flying time — you're only in the air for 5.5 hours.
flaws.why_tempting: 8:30 to 5:00 is instant clock subtraction, and you already mentioned the 3-hour difference on line 2, so your brain thinks it accounted for it.
flaws.catch_rule: Before subtracting departure and arrival times, put both clocks in the same time zone.
flaws.hint: When the plane lifts off at 8:30 AM in San Francisco, what time is it in Boston?

practice.problem: A flight leaves New York at 6:00 PM local and lands in Los Angeles (3 hours behind) at 9:15 PM local. How long is the flight?
practice.answer: 6 hours 15 minutes — 6:00 PM in NY is 3:00 PM in LA, and 3:00 PM to 9:15 PM is 6h 15m.

diagnosis: Airlines always print arrival times in the departure city's time zone, so 5:00 PM is still Pacific time.
No nonstop flight from San Francisco to Boston takes off in the morning and lands at 5:00 PM.
Local takeoff and landing times already include TSA security wait time at the airport.
8:30 AM to 5:00 PM crosses noon, so you can't subtract them without converting to 24-hour time.
fix: Check the itinerary — 5:00 PM is probably San Francisco time, not Boston time.
Confirm the flight doesn't have a hidden 3-hour layover in Chicago.
Add two hours at the airport before 8:30 AM to get the real trip length.

diagnosis: Boston is three hours behind San Francisco, not ahead, so you actually gain three hours of afternoon.
Because of daylight saving time, the gap between California and Massachusetts is only two hours.
Losing three hours means you lose half the day on the return flight too, not just going east.
Being three hours ahead only affects your watch after you land, not the flight duration.
fix: Flip it: Boston is 3 hours behind San Francisco, so you'll land with extra afternoon.
Check whether Boston is 2 or 3 hours ahead in November.
Note that the 3-hour shift changes how long the flight feels, not the 8.5-hour airtime.
Set your watch to Boston time only after stepping off the plane.

diagnosis: On an 8.5-hour daytime flight, an aisle seat is way better than a window seat for stretching.
Window seats on eastbound flights face the sun all morning, making movies hard to watch.
Grabbing a window seat won't stop the plane from taking 11.5 hours with the time change.
Four movies only fill 6 hours, so even with a window seat you'll be bored for 2.5 hours.
fix: Switch to an aisle seat for an 8.5-hour flight.
Download a podcast too for the extra 2.5 hours after four movies.
Pick the left side of the plane to stay out of the sun.
Bring a charger since four movies will drain your tablet.

Boston is three hours ahead of San Francisco, so I'm losing most of the afternoon once I land.
8:30 AM in San Francisco is already 11:30 AM in Boston, so landing at 5:00 PM local is only 5.5 hours in the air, not 8.5.
At least I grabbed a window seat.
clean_conclusion: 8:30 AM in San Francisco is already 11:30 AM in Boston — you're only in the air for 5.5 hours, not 8.5.
